chunks: And it is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “It was mentioned to us that a man from the Anṣār died while owing two dinars as a debt, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not pray over him and said, ‘Pray over your brother,’ until one of his relatives guaranteed them on his behalf.”
So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “That is the truth.”

Then he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم only did that so that they might take admonition, and so that some of them would respond for others, and so that they would not treat debt lightly. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم died while he had debt, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was killed while he had debt, and al-Ḥasan عليه السلام died while he had debt, and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام was killed while he had debt.”

key_terms.بِالدَّيْنِ: with respect to debt and financial obligation
key_terms.دَيْنًا: a financial debt owed by a person
key_terms.دِينَارَانِ: two dinars, specifying the amount of the debt
key_terms.ضَمِنَهُمَا: guaranteed the two dinars on his behalf
key_terms.لِيَتَّعِظُوا: so that they may take admonition and learn a lesson

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم refrain from praying over someone who died in debt?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم withheld leading the funeral prayer of a debtor until the debt was guaranteed, and Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام affirms the report. He explains that this was done as a moral lesson so people would take debts seriously and support one another, not because debt itself negates the dignity of the righteous, as even the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the Imams عليهم السلام had debts at their deaths.
